newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Treasury posts operational deficit in July.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Treasury posts operational deficit in July.

text.p: Brazil's National Treasury posted an operational deficit of 663 million reais in July, the Treasury said in a statement.

The Treasury said the July result brought its operational deficit for the year so far to 3.153 billion reais or the equivalent of 0.64 percent of gross domestic product, compared with a 0.42 percent deficit in January-July last year.

The operational figure includes payment of interest on debt. Treasury budget figures reflect only spending by the federal government and not the consolidated accounts of the whole public sector, which are released every month by the Central Bank.
The Treasury said its July primary result, which does not include debt-servicing costs, was a 576 million reais surplus.

For the seven-month period, the primary surplus stood at 4.715 billion reais or 0.96 percent of gross domestic product compared with a surplus of 3.851 billion reais or 0.82 percent of GDP in January-July 1996.
Total receipts in July were 9.194 billion reais while normal expenditure amounted to 8.618 billion reais.
Interest payments in July were 1.239 billion reais while payroll costs for the month were 4.271 billion reais.
